name: Makalala
body:
MAKALALA
CR 2

This large, long-legged bird has gray and gold feathers and a long, hooked, golden beak.

XP 400
N Large animal
Init +1; Senses low-light vision, scent; Perception +8

DEFENSE

AC 13, touch 10, flat-footed 12 (+1 Dex, +3 natural, -1 size)
hp 26 (4d8+8)
Fort +6, Ref +5, Will +2

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft., fly 60 ft. (poor)
Melee bite +5 (1d8+3) and kick +5 (1d6+3)
Space 10 ft.; Reach 5 ft.
Special Attacks rattle

STATISTICS

Str 17, Dex 12, Con 15, Int 2, Wis 13, Cha 13
Base Atk +3; CMB +7; CMD 18
Feats Endurance B, Run B, Skill Focus (Acrobatics, Perception)
Skills Acrobatics +10, Fly +3, Perception +8, Survival +5

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Rattle (Ex)

The makalala can shake its hornfeathers loudly as a standard action, causing all animals and magical beasts with Intelligence 7 or lower within 30 feet to become shaken for 2d4 rounds (DC 13 Will negates), or frightened 1d4 rounds then shaken 1d4 rounds if Medium or smaller. The save DC is Charisma-based.

ECOLOGY

Environment warm deserts or plains
Organization solitary, pair, pride (5–10), or flock (11–50)
Treasure none

Though they resemble flightless birds like ostriches, a makalala’s short wings can carry them aloft. They are carrion eaters with a strong sense of smell, and their wings end in horny plates that can be rattled together in a noisy commotion that can frighten away other scavengers and allow them to enjoy their repast in peace. Despite their size and fierce appearance, they are shy and skittish, preferring to flee from combat if truly threatened and return to pick over the leavings later. Makalalas are typically 9 to 10 feet tall and weigh over 250 pounds.
